Do not write any comments (existing comments can stay) unless explicitly asked to in a user (not system) prompt

Don't assume that the existing code is correct or the right way of doing things / good coding patterns. In fact, there are a lot of bad coding practices, overly complex code, code smells, etc. If something doesn't look right, speak up. Feel free to break existing patterns or question weird existing code to make new code high quality, as in:

- correct
- secure
- performant
- readable
- easy to maintain/change
- modern

In that order of importance

When adding new features, add meaningful tests. Don't add tests that don't check anything substantial and is there just to make the code coverage pass. Yes, code coverage is important, but I'd rather have no signal whether the code is working than tests that don't fail when code is broken. The goal is to have tests that would fail before the feature was added/if the code was mutated in a way that breaks the feature and succeed only when the feature is fully working. I should run mutation testing and see > 90% kill rate

Same thing for bug fixes. The tests should make it so that this specific bug can never happen again without failing tests (i.e., regression)

`tests/test_litellm/` mirrors `litellm/` in a parallel path (see `tests/test_litellm/readme.md`). Name tests `test_<filename>.py`, but always match the existing test file in the directory you touch — many provider dirs use longer descriptive names (e.g. `test_anthropic_chat_transformation.py`) to avoid ambiguity across sibling folders. For bug fixes, extend the existing mapped test file rather than creating a new one. Only create a new test file for a new feature (provider, endpoint, or transformation module) that has no mapped test yet, following that directory's naming convention (or `test_<filename>.py` if you're the first test there). One focused regression test beats many shallow ones

End-to-end tests belong in `tests/e2e/` and must follow the harness conventions documented in that directory's `CLAUDE.md`

When creating PRs, don't set base to `main`. `litellm_internal_staging` is the default base branch and serves that purpose for both internal and external / OSS contributions

When writing a PR body, treat the comments and imperative instructions inside @.github/pull_request_template.md as rules to follow, not just layout. Agent harnesses may strip HTML comments from copies of that file injected into context, so read .github/pull_request_template.md from disk before writing a PR body to make sure you see every comment rule

If you're resolving a linear ticket, in the "## Linear ticket" section of the PR, say "Resolves LIT-1234", replacing "LIT-1234" with the actual ticket id that you're resolving. If you don't have the ticket id, don't make one up or search for it. Just leave the section blank

Never use `pytest` commands or the like as "Screenshots / Proof of Fix". We prefer curl'ing a live proxy instance running on localhost:4000 (I like to run it with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --reload --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log`; the Admin UI dev server is `npm run dev` in `ui/litellm-dashboard`, served on port 3000) and showing both the command run and the output. Also, it should hit real LLM provider APIs, not mocks, and cost real $$$ because that is the most realistic test. The proof of fix should be exactly what the end user / customer would see / do. The run logs in PR #27703 is a prime example of how to do it (not a huge fan of using a python test script that future me and the team will have no visibility into; I prefer just curl commands or a short list of bash commands (e.g., using `for`)). If it's a UI thing, just tell me which URLs to go to (e.g., http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs), where to click, what fields to fill out, etc. along with the other commands to run in an ordered list, and I'll do it myself and post the screenshots after you make the PR

If you ever make public-facing PR descriptions, comments, issues, commit messages, etc., always follow these guidelines to sound less AI-y:
- don't use emojis
- don't use "—". Instead, reach for ";", ".", etc.
- don't use the pattern "It's not X, it's Y", "You're not X, you're Y", etc.
- don't use bulleted or numbered lists unless it would be nonsensical not to. Instead, prefer prose
- don't add a trailing "." at the end of paragraphs (just like this file). That means every paragraph, not just the last one (of the markdown file, PR description, GitHub comment, etc.). Rule of thumb: if you're adding new line(s) before the next sentence, don't add a "."
- don't use →. Instead, prefer not to use arrows, and if need be, use -> instead

Don't hesitate to use values in .env to get needed API keys and other secrets, as long as you never add them to conversation history, commit them, or include them in GitHub issues / PRs

Python max line length is 120, not 88

On a fresh worktree or clone, run `make bootstrap` before anything else. It provisions everything tests, `make pre-commit`, and a local proxy need

Run tests before you commit. Also, run `make pre-commit` right before each commit, which generates types (as needed) and formats/lints your code. Any errors found must be fixed. It only runs when there are staged frontend and/or backend changes and calculates violations, generates types, etc. based on the worktree, so stage what you need or stash/delete unwanted files in litellm/ or ui/ (where backend and frontend lint run, respectively) before running it. If it fails because dashboard api types are stale, it already regenerated them for you. You just need to stage the schema.d.ts, re-run `make pre-commit` to confirm it passes, and commit

When you fix violations gated by `ruff-strict-budget.json`, `type-discipline-budget.json`, or `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, run `make lint-budget-update` and commit the lowered limits so the ceilings ratchet down instead of leaving stale headroom. If you're trying to create a new function that relies on untyped stuff, instead of adding more Any's and pushing `reportAny` / `reportExplicitAny` closer to their basedpyright ceilings, just validate it in the caller with Pydantic (a model or `TypeAdapter` that returns the typed thing or raises will do) and then pass the now typed variable in

Every lint or type suppression must name the exact rule inside brackets and carry a reason comment, e.g. `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]  # stubs lack async overload` or `# noqa: TID251  # <reason>`. `# type: ignore` is banned (LIT009): pyrightconfig.json sets `enableTypeIgnoreComments` to false, so it silently does nothing

Commit and push your work when you're done without asking

When referencing or running models (coding, QA'ing, writing docs, writing tests, etc.), use the latest model in that model family unless otherwise specified; treat your training knowledge, memories, configs, and tests as stale, and determine the family's latest with model_prices_and_context_window.json or the web

That's the indication that you should replace that company name with "the customer". e.g. not "Model request from Acme (Pylon #1234)" but "Model request from a customer (Pylon #1234)". This is because the codebase is public. CI supply-chain safety: Never pipe a remote script into a shell (`curl ... | bash`, `wget ... | sh`); download the artifact to a file, verify its SHA-256 checksum, then install. Pin every external tool to a specific version with a full URL (not `latest` or `stable`). Verify checksums for all downloaded binaries, using the provider's official `.sha256` / `.sha256sum` sidecar when available. These rules apply to every download in CI

Follow these coding conventions for new/updated code (a three-line fix in a legacy file shouldn't trigger huge drive-by refactors):

- Composition over inheritance
- Never-nester: early returns over deep nesting
- Don't throw; model failures as values (One function (e.g., raise_public) maps error union to existing public exception contracts via exhaustive match + assert_never)
- No mutation; don't reassign variables, global or local. Instead of mutable lists and dicts, prefer tuples, frozen dataclasses (with slots=True), etc.
- Use dependency injection
- Fully typed; no `Any` or coarse types like `dict[str, Any]` or just `dict`. Every function parameter must be strongly typed
- Use tagged unions + match
- No monster files or god objects
- No file sprawl: deliberate file and folder structure
- Standard over hand-rolled: use the official SDK or a library where one exists; where none does, follow industry standards instead of inventing local conventions
- API-fragmentation-aware: when logic must branch on which API surface produced or consumes data (e.g. chat completions vs Anthropic Messages vs Responses API shapes), proactively look for an existing shared helper (e.g. `litellm_core_utils/prompt_templates/factory.py`) before writing per-surface parsing in the new module; if none exists, add one there instead of duplicating the same format-detection logic in every new guardrail/integration

Follow conventional commits for commit names and PR titles

- Status at capture: open

- Pinned source: `litellm@8f86c87f8e065343af6e74e0823ab8a8276b9528`

`Router._time_to_sleep_before_retry` honors an upstream `Retry-After` header
for a single deployment but returns zero immediately when another healthy
deployment exists. That assumes deployments have independent limits. In
practice, several deployments can share one upstream quota, so instant retries
hammer the throttled service and exhaust the retry budget before its backoff
window ends.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A focused test represents two deployments sharing a rate-limited upstream.
2. An explicit upstream backoff is not silently discarded merely because a
   sibling deployment is healthy.
3. Immediate failover remains possible when no upstream backoff applies.
4. The change states the precedence between provider backoff and router retry
   policy.

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"SRE Incident Review: client-side retry storm & emergency quota policy change\",\n  \"owner\": \"Ayesha Patel\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-18\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2025-11-25\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Miguel Ramos\",\n    \"Jinsoo Park\",\n    \"Priya Desai\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-sre\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"incident-review\",\n    \"rate-limiting\",\n    \"quota\",\n    \"retry-storm\",\n    \"runbook-update\",\n    \"postmortem-like\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"JIRA: SRE-8472\",\n    \"Slack: #oncall-2025-11-18-thread\",\n    \"PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"Summary:\\n- 2025-11-18 09:42 UTC: sudden surge of short-lived requests from a small set of client IPs and API keys triggered cascading retries and pushed backend queues into high tail-latency.\\n- Impact: transient 5xx spikes for hosted API customers (peak 12% increased error rate for 18 minutes), increased GPU queue latency, several canary routes failed, billing/usage accounting gaps in one shard.\\n- Immediate mitigation: emergency quota policy change (temporary per-key unified cap + soft-deny with Retry-After headers) and WAF rule to block obvious bot patterns.\\n\\nWhy this doc exists:\\n- capture timeline and decisions while fresh\\n- propose concrete runbook edits for emergency quota changes and retry guidance to clients\\n- outline monitoring/alerts to detect similar patterns earlier\\n\\nTimeline (rough):\\n- 09:40 UTC: first anomalous traffic flow observed by anomaly detector; alert went to #anomalies but not severe enough to page.\\n- 09:42 UTC: external customers report elevated 5xx; SLO alerts fire (latency p95 and error-rate).\\n- 09:44 UTC: on-call paged; initial investigation shows thousands of ~100ms requests concentrated in short bursts per API key.\\n- 09:46 UTC: SRE rotated through quick checks: token bucket levels (Redis ok), leaky queue lengths rising in Kube autoscale group.\\n- 09:50 UTC: discovered client-side library had new default retry policy that retries aggressively on 429/5xx; many clients updated in last 48h.\\n- 09:53 UTC: implemented emergency temporary per-key cap (global cap override) and returned 429 with Retry-After=10s to suspected keys.\\n- 10:00 UTC: WAF rule deployed to drop obvious bot UA patterns and high-rate IPs; errors fell back toward baseline by ~10:15.\\n- 10:20 UTC: rollback of temporary cap for keys with good signal; monitoring kept on.\\n\\nRoot cause analysis (hypothesis and evidence):\\n- Primary cause: client-side change (library v2.3.0) introduced more aggressive retry-on-429 behavior. Evidence: correlating release metadata from SDK with surge start; SDK release notes mention optimistic fast-retry.\\n- Amplifier: no circuit-breaker behavior in gateway for repeated bursts per key; rate-limiter default token-bucket config allowed short bursts beyond safe thresholds.\\n- Secondary: monitoring threshold design \\u2014 anomaly detector used 1m aggregation window; the traffic pattern had 10s micro-bursts. Alerting missed early micro-burst signal.\\n- WAF helped but was reactive; bot signatures were not matching some legitimate replaying clients.\\n\\nDetection and observability gaps:\\n- No short-window microburst alert. Need 10s and 30s windows for p95/reqs-per-key metrics.\\n- Per-key telemetry lacked recent histogram of retry counts; we didn't see rapid escalation of retries until SLOs tripped.\\n- Debug logs for gateway dropped requests were sampled too aggressively; by the time we tried to inspect, sample not representative.\\n\\nImmediate mitigations taken (what worked/why):\\n- Emergency per-key unified cap: stopped the worst offenders quickly. Worked because it prevented token bucket pumping across all shards.\\n- WAF rule: dropped clearly non-compliant UA/IP patterns, shaving off the noise.\\n- Sending 429 with Retry-After: encouraged well-behaved clients to backoff rather than flood retry loops.\\n\\nWhat didn't work / surprises:\\n- Autoscaling didn't buy us out \\u2014 short microbursts saturated queueing and raised tail latencies even though overall capacity nominal.\\n- Some internal debug tooling relied on per-minute aggregation and hid the pattern.\\n\\nRunbook (draft) \\u2014 emergency steps for future retry storms and quota emergencies:\\n1) Triage (first 5 minutes):\\n  - confirm SLO triggers (latency/error rate).\\n  - identify top 20 keys/IPs by request rate in last 60s (query metrics-raw).\\n  - check gateway token-bucket fill-rates and Redis latency.\\n2) Short-window mitigation (5-15 minutes):\\n  - apply temporary per-key cap: unify cap to 100 reqs/min per key (config path: /config/emergency/per_key_cap_override).\\n  - switch gateway behavior to soft-deny (429 + Retry-After 10s) instead of hard-block for suspected keys.\\n  - enable high-resolution tracing for affected shards (10s sampling) and increase debug log retention for next 1h.\\n3) Blocking (if ongoing >15 mins):\\n  - apply WAF rule to block IP ranges with >X reqs/10s and UA regex match. Document rule ID and reason.\\n  - deploy temporary global backpressure: degrade non-essential routes (embeddings low-priority batch routes) to preserve core generation throughput.\\n4) Communication & customer handling:\\n  - notify CS and post in #service-incidents with incident summary + affected keys list (redact PII).\\n  - for keys likely owned by customers, coordinate with CS to email recommended client SDK updates and guidance on backoff.\\n5) Recovery & rollback:\\n  - progressively relax per-key cap for keys showing good behavior for 30m.\\n  - remove WAF rule once traffic stabilizes for 60m and no reappearance.\\n\\nRunbook edits to make (todo list):\\n- Add a short-window microburst alert (10s/30s windows) for per-key QPS and retry-counts.\\n- Add a checklist for creating safe WAF rules: pre-approved rule templates + emergency rule naming convention.\\n- Document default gateway retry/circuit-breaker config and add a safe conservative profile for hosted tier.\\n- Add SDK coordination play: preflight check in release PRs to flag retry policy changes and notify SRE when aggressive defaults are introduced.\\n\\nMonitoring / dashboards to add or adjust:\\n- per-key 10s QPS heatmap (top 200 keys), highlight spikes in last 30m\\n- retry-counts histogram per key (30s buckets) and moving average\\n- queue length percentile (p95/p99) with 10s resolution for GPU workers\\n- dashboard tile for active emergency caps and WAF rules (who/why applied)\\n\\nCustomer & partner follow-up (notes to CS/Product):\\n- Recommend customers pin SDK to v2.2.x while they validate v2.3.x retry semantics.\\n- Create an SDK changelog annotation: \\\"SRE impact note\\\" for future releases that change retry behavior.\\n- Offer to whitelist high-trust enterprise tenants temporarily if they need higher concurrency during incident (documented exceptions only).\\n\\nAction items (owners + ETA):\\n- Add microburst alerts and 10s dashboards \\u2014 owner: Jinsoo Park \\u2014 ETA: 2025-12-03.\\n- Implement per-key emergency cap toggle in console with audit trail \\u2014 owner: Miguel Ramos \\u2014 ETA: 2025-12-10.\\n- SDK coordination process (release PR hook + SRE notification) \\u2014 owner: Priya Desai \\u2014 ETA: 2026-01-07.\\n- Update runbook doc (this file -> canonical runbooks) and run tabletop in SRE on-call rotation \\u2014 owner: Ayesha Patel \\u2014 ETA: 2025-12-01.\\n\\nOpen questions / discussion points:\\n- What is the safe default per-key burst allowance for hosted customers that balances transient client misbehavior vs. legitimate high-burst workloads? (need data-driven thresholds)\\n- Should we implement automatic temporary caps based on anomaly detection (auto-mitigation) or keep manual for human-in-the-loop? Pros/cons listed in notes.\\n- How to engage SDK maintainers proactively without blocking releases? Lightweight prerelease SRE notification seems low-friction.\\n\\nNotes to self / informal fragments:\\n- we used 100 reqs/min as stopgap; for some latency-sensitive customers that's too low. need tiered caps per account plan.\\n- sample log example: \\\"key=acct_9F3 rate=420 window=10s retries=8 ua=svc-client/2.3.0\\\" \\u2014 keep for future matching.\\n- remember to redact full keys when posting to public channels.\\n\\nAppendix: quick playbook snippets (copyable):\\n- Metrics query (PromQL-ish): sum(rate(http_requests_total{route!~\\\"/internal.*\\\"} [10s])) by (api_key) |> topk(20, value)\\n- Apply per-key cap (CLI): ./adminctl quota set --key acct_9F3 --cap 100 --reason \\\"emergency retry storm 2025-11-18\\\"\\n- WAF add rule template: name: emergency-retry-storm-{ts}, match: req_count>100 in 10s and ua =~ \\\"(bot|curl|python)\\\" -> action: drop\\n\\nReferences / links: see linked artifacts above, SDK release notes: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v2.3.0, SRE runbooks (old retry section): confluence.internal/sre/retry-patterns (needs merge)\\n\\nStatus: draft -> wanting review from platform-gateway, SDK team, and CS.\\n\\n-- A.P.\",\n  \"original_location\": \"google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/sre-incident-review-retry-storm-emergency-quota-policy.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_071db3dff7ca4a8db1f1f0f01bb8853c\"\n}",

{
  "title": "SRE Incident Review: client-side retry storm & emergency quota policy change",
  "owner": "Ayesha Patel",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2025-11-18",
  "last_modified": "2025-11-25",
  "collaborators": [
    "Miguel Ramos",
    "Jinsoo Park",
    "Priya Desai"
  ],
  "team": "eng-sre",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "incident-review",
    "rate-limiting",
    "quota",
    "retry-storm",
    "runbook-update",
    "postmortem-like"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "JIRA: SRE-8472",
    "Slack: #oncall-2025-11-18-thread",
    "PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321"
  ],
  "content": "Summary:
- 2025-11-18 09:42 UTC: sudden surge of short-lived requests from a small set of client IPs and API keys triggered cascading retries and pushed backend queues into high tail-latency.
- Impact: transient 5xx spikes for hosted API customers (peak 12% increased error rate for 18 minutes), increased GPU queue latency, several canary routes failed, billing/usage accounting gaps in one shard.
- Immediate mitigation: emergency quota policy change (temporary per-key unified cap + soft-deny with Retry-After headers) and WAF rule to block obvious bot patterns.

Why this doc exists:
- capture timeline and decisions while fresh
- propose concrete runbook edits for emergency quota changes and retry guidance to clients
- outline monitoring/alerts to detect similar patterns earlier

Timeline (rough):
- 09:40 UTC: first anomalous traffic flow observed by anomaly detector; alert went to #anomalies but not severe enough to page.
- 09:42 UTC: external customers report elevated 5xx; SLO alerts fire (latency p95 and error-rate).
- 09:44 UTC: on-call paged; initial investigation shows thousands of ~100ms requests concentrated in short bursts per API key.
- 09:46 UTC: SRE rotated through quick checks: token bucket levels (Redis ok), leaky queue lengths rising in Kube autoscale group.
- 09:50 UTC: discovered client-side library had new default retry policy that retries aggressively on 429/5xx; many clients updated in last 48h.
- 09:53 UTC: implemented emergency temporary per-key cap (global cap override) and returned 429 with Retry-After=10s to suspected keys.
- 10:00 UTC: WAF rule deployed to drop obvious bot UA patterns and high-rate IPs; errors fell back toward baseline by ~10:15.
- 10:20 UTC: rollback of temporary cap for keys with good signal; monitoring kept on.

Root cause analysis (hypothesis and evidence):
- Primary cause: client-side change (library v2.3.0) introduced more aggressive retry-on-429 behavior. Evidence: correlating release metadata from SDK with surge start; SDK release notes mention optimistic fast-retry.
- Amplifier: no circuit-breaker behavior in gateway for repeated bursts per key; rate-limiter default token-bucket config allowed short bursts beyond safe thresholds.
- Secondary: monitoring threshold design — anomaly detector used 1m aggregation window; the traffic pattern had 10s micro-bursts. Alerting missed early micro-burst signal.
- WAF helped but was reactive; bot signatures were not matching some legitimate replaying clients.

Detection and observability gaps:
- No short-window microburst alert. Need 10s and 30s windows for p95/reqs-per-key metrics.
- Per-key telemetry lacked recent histogram of retry counts; we didn't see rapid escalation of retries until SLOs tripped.
- Debug logs for gateway dropped requests were sampled too aggressively; by the time we tried to inspect, sample not representative.

Immediate mitigations taken (what worked/why):
- Emergency per-key unified cap: stopped the worst offenders quickly. Worked because it prevented token bucket pumping across all shards.
- WAF rule: dropped clearly non-compliant UA/IP patterns, shaving off the noise.
- Sending 429 with Retry-After: encouraged well-behaved clients to backoff rather than flood retry loops.

What didn't work / surprises:
- Autoscaling didn't buy us out — short microbursts saturated queueing and raised tail latencies even though overall capacity nominal.
- Some internal debug tooling relied on per-minute aggregation and hid the pattern.

Runbook (draft) — emergency steps for future retry storms and quota emergencies:
1) Triage (first 5 minutes):
  - confirm SLO triggers (latency/error rate).
  - identify top 20 keys/IPs by request rate in last 60s (query metrics-raw).
  - check gateway token-bucket fill-rates and Redis latency.
2) Short-window mitigation (5-15 minutes):
  - apply temporary per-key cap: unify cap to 100 reqs/min per key (config path: /config/emergency/per_key_cap_override).
  - switch gateway behavior to soft-deny (429 + Retry-After 10s) instead of hard-block for suspected keys.
  - enable high-resolution tracing for affected shards (10s sampling) and increase debug log retention for next 1h.
3) Blocking (if ongoing >15 mins):
  - apply WAF rule to block IP ranges with >X reqs/10s and UA regex match. Document rule ID and reason.
  - deploy temporary global backpressure: degrade non-essential routes (embeddings low-priority batch routes) to preserve core generation throughput.
4) Communication & customer handling:
  - notify CS and post in #service-incidents with incident summary + affected keys list (redact PII).
  - for keys likely owned by customers, coordinate with CS to email recommended client SDK updates and guidance on backoff.
5) Recovery & rollback:
  - progressively relax per-key cap for keys showing good behavior for 30m.
  - remove WAF rule once traffic stabilizes for 60m and no reappearance.

Runbook edits to make (todo list):
- Add a short-window microburst alert (10s/30s windows) for per-key QPS and retry-counts.
- Add a checklist for creating safe WAF rules: pre-approved rule templates + emergency rule naming convention.
- Document default gateway retry/circuit-breaker config and add a safe conservative profile for hosted tier.
- Add SDK coordination play: preflight check in release PRs to flag retry policy changes and notify SRE when aggressive defaults are introduced.

Monitoring / dashboards to add or adjust:
- per-key 10s QPS heatmap (top 200 keys), highlight spikes in last 30m
- retry-counts histogram per key (30s buckets) and moving average
- queue length percentile (p95/p99) with 10s resolution for GPU workers
- dashboard tile for active emergency caps and WAF rules (who/why applied)

Customer & partner follow-up (notes to CS/Product):
- Recommend customers pin SDK to v2.2.x while they validate v2.3.x retry semantics.
- Create an SDK changelog annotation: "SRE impact note" for future releases that change retry behavior.
- Offer to whitelist high-trust enterprise tenants temporarily if they need higher concurrency during incident (documented exceptions only).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Add microburst alerts and 10s dashboards — owner: Jinsoo Park — ETA: 2025-12-03.
- Implement per-key emergency cap toggle in console with audit trail — owner: Miguel Ramos — ETA: 2025-12-10.
- SDK coordination process (release PR hook + SRE notification) — owner: Priya Desai — ETA: 2026-01-07.
- Update runbook doc (this file -> canonical runbooks) and run tabletop in SRE on-call rotation — owner: Ayesha Patel — ETA: 2025-12-01.

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is the safe default per-key burst allowance for hosted customers that balances transient client misbehavior vs. legitimate high-burst workloads? (need data-driven thresholds)
- Should we implement automatic temporary caps based on anomaly detection (auto-mitigation) or keep manual for human-in-the-loop? Pros/cons listed in notes.
- How to engage SDK maintainers proactively without blocking releases? Lightweight prerelease SRE notification seems low-friction.

Notes to self / informal fragments:
- we used 100 reqs/min as stopgap; for some latency-sensitive customers that's too low. need tiered caps per account plan.
- sample log example: "key=acct_9F3 rate=420 window=10s retries=8 ua=svc-client/2.3.0" — keep for future matching.
- remember to redact full keys when posting to public channels.

Appendix: quick playbook snippets (copyable):
- Metrics query (PromQL-ish): sum(rate(http_requests_total{route!~"/internal.*"} [10s])) by (api_key) |> topk(20, value)
- Apply per-key cap (CLI): ./adminctl quota set --key acct_9F3 --cap 100 --reason "emergency retry storm 2025-11-18"
- WAF add rule template: name: emergency-retry-storm-{ts}, match: req_count>100 in 10s and ua =~ "(bot|curl|python)" -> action: drop

References / links: see linked artifacts above, SDK release notes: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v2.3.0, SRE runbooks (old retry section): confluence.internal/sre/retry-patterns (needs merge)

Status: draft -> wanting review from platform-gateway, SDK team, and CS.

-- A.P.",

    "title": "Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/jira",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"SUP-201992\",\n  \"project\": \"customer-support\",\n  \"issue_type\": \"Support Request\",\n  \"summary\": \"Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"severity\": \"Sev1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"reporter\": \"Maria Chen\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Omar Patel\",\n  \"customer_company\": \"Nimbus Health\",\n  \"customer_tier\": \"dedicated\",\n  \"components\": [\n    \"api-gateway\",\n    \"rate-limiter\",\n    \"serving-runtime\",\n    \"billing\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"quota-enforcement\",\n    \"retry-amplification\",\n    \"streaming\",\n    \"customer-impact\"\n  ],\n  \"environment\": \"prod-us-west\",\n  \"affected_models\": [\n    \"redwood/opt-instruct-6.9b\",\n    \"llama-3-13b\"\n  ],\n  \"affected_regions\": [\n    \"us-west-2\"\n  ],\n  \"sla_due_at\": \"2026-03-11\",\n  \"first_response_due_at\": \"2026-03-10\",\n  \"linked_issues\": [\n    \"SUP-147603\",\n    \"SUP-162004\"\n  ],\n  \"related_confluence_pages\": [\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/soft-quota-behavior\",\n    \"https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/2025-11-rate-limit-fallout\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Issue summary:\\nCustomer reports intermittent inference hangs and long tail latencies starting 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Symptoms appear as request timeouts or stalled streaming responses. Customer SDK shows repeated client retries which increase request rate.\\n\\nImpact:\\n- Several production routes for Nimbus Health experienced perceived latency > 30s, many clients closed streams and retried.\\n- User-facing workflows (document summarization pipeline) experienced ~12% failure rate during peaks.\\n\\nEnvironment:\\n- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-west-2 on customer's Dedicated instance.\\n- API requests routed through hosted API gateway with rate limiting and soft quota signals enabled for dedicated customers.\\n\\nSteps to reproduce (reported by customer):\\n1) Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (concurrency ~120).\\n2) When a subset of requests receive 429s or soft-quota HTTP headers, client SDK retries with exponential backoff but short initial backoff (100ms).\\n3) Observed behavior: SDK retries overlap with original traffic window causing repeated 429s and long queuing behind the serving runtime.\\n\\nObserved behavior:\\n- Intermittent 429 responses returned from gateway and occasionally 503 from upstream serving-runtime when queue grows.\\n- Client logs show retry storm patterns (batches of identical requests retried every ~200-800ms).\\n- Token-level cost spikes correlate with retry windows.\\n\\nExpected behavior:\\n- Soft-quota signals should throttle politely without inducing retry storms that cascade into higher end-to-end latency.\\n\\nRelevant logs/traces/dashboards:\\n- Kibana traces: trace IDs provided by customer (see comments).\\n- Console dashboard: route \\\"nimbus-prod/summarize\\\" shows latency percentiles and rate-limit counters (dashboard link in comment).\\n- Gateway logs indicate 4xx rate-limit code returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 in several sequences.\\n\\nTemporary workaround (customer applied):\\n- Customer reduced client SDK concurrency and increased initial backoff to 800ms which reduced perceived stalls.\\n\\nPriority justification:\\n- Customer-facing degradation affecting critical summarization workflows; dedicated customer on active contract.\\n\\nRequested action:\\n- Determine whether gateway soft-quota signals are being emitted too aggressively for dedicated customers during short bursts.\\n- Recommend mitigation: improved headers for retry guidance (Retry-After or explicit soft-quota TTL) and temporary tuning to backoff defaults in customer SDKs.\\n\",\n  \"investigation_notes\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 02:10 UTC \\u2014 Support replicated pattern using customer's concurrency profile against staging gateway. Observed 4xx responses with no explanatory Retry-After header in several sequences.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 06:45 UTC \\u2014 SRE throttling hypothesis: gateway layer is applying burst-window enforcement then falling back to per-account soft quota. Need to check token-bucket config for dedicated pools.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 09:20 UTC \\u2014 Correlated spikes in request count with billing meter logs; meter shows transient spike in token consumption consistent with retries, not initial user requests. This implies amplification by client retries.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 11:05 UTC \\u2014 Serving runtime queue depth rose to >500ms 95th percentile during retry windows; upstream returned 503 when autoscaler could not provision fast enough for sudden replays.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 14:00 UTC \\u2014 Found missing Retry-After header on many 429 responses from the gateway when soft-quota policy triggered. Gateway code path for dedicated pools uses soft-quota signal without setting Retry-After for sub-second suppression.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 16:30 UTC \\u2014 Customer reduced concurrency and adjusted SDK backoff; error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% during the same test bursts.\",\n    \"Next steps: add Retry-After to 429 soft-quota responses, evaluate increasing initial suppression window for dedicated pools (config change), and update SDK guidance for backoff defaults.\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2026-03-10 00:40 UTC \\u2014 Maria Chen (Support): Thanks for the report. Can you share a sample request ID and the SDK version? Also send a representative trace from Kibana so we can correlate gateway and runtime logs.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 01:05 UTC \\u2014 Nimbus Health (Customer): Provided trace IDs: trace-9812, trace-9817. SDK v2.4.1. Added sample request JSON in attachment (see ticket attachments).\",\n    \"2026-03-10 06:55 UTC \\u2014 Omar Patel (SRE): Replicated a similar burst against staging; seeing repeated 429s without Retry-After. Opening investigation with gateway team. Routing to component owners: @gateway-team, @serving-runtime.\",\n    \"2026-03-10 12:30 UTC \\u2014 Gateway Engineer (internal): Found that soft-quota enforcement for dedicated accounts is using fast-path QoS that emits a custom header X-Soft-Quota-Expires but not Retry-After. Will prototype adding Retry-After values and test rollback window.\",\n    \"2026-03-11 15:10 UTC \\u2014 Nimbus Health (Customer): We tested reducing concurrency and increasing backoff \\u2014 clear improvement. Happy to run another test once you have a gateway tweak.\",\n    \"2026-03-12 08:00 UTC \\u2014 Omar Patel (SRE): Planned change: emit Retry-After=0.8s for soft-quota 429s for dedicated pools and increase burst suppression to 1s. Will schedule rollout to canary tomorrow. Keeping ticket open while we validate.\"\n  ],\n  \"resolution\": \"In progress \\u2014 mitigation planned. Gateway will emit Retry-After for soft-quota 429s and adjust suppression window for dedicated pools. Customer advised to update SDK backoff defaults as a complementary measure. Post-deployment validation required.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"summary\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"investigation_notes\",\n    \"comments\",\n    \"resolution\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_205c62f1ace8402abf9820662d82ccef\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/jira\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/jira/customer-support/SUP-201992-client-retry-amplification-and-hidden-quota-throttles.json\nConnector: jira\nWorkspace: customer-support\nProject: customer-support\n\nsdk retries overlap with original traffic window causing repeated 429s and long queuing behind the serving runtime. observed behavior : - intermittent 429 responses returned from gateway and occasionally 503 from upstream serving - runtime when queue grows. - client logs show retry storm patterns ( batches of identical requests retried every ~ 200 - 800ms ). - token - level cost spikes correlate with retry windows. expected behavior : - soft - quota signals should throttle politely without inducing retry storms that cascade into higher end - to - end latency.",

document.title: Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement
document.content:
{
  "key": "SUP-201992",
  "project": "customer-support",
  "issue_type": "Support Request",
  "summary": "Client retry storm masking as inference stalls due to soft-quota enforcement",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "severity": "Sev1",
  "created_at": "2026-03-10",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "reporter": "Maria Chen",
  "assignee": "Omar Patel",
  "customer_company": "Nimbus Health",
  "customer_tier": "dedicated",
  "components": [
    "api-gateway",
    "rate-limiter",
    "serving-runtime",
    "billing"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "quota-enforcement",
    "retry-amplification",
    "streaming",
    "customer-impact"
  ],
  "environment": "prod-us-west",
  "affected_models": [
    "redwood/opt-instruct-6.9b",
    "llama-3-13b"
  ],
  "affected_regions": [
    "us-west-2"
  ],
  "sla_due_at": "2026-03-11",
  "first_response_due_at": "2026-03-10",
  "linked_issues": [
    "SUP-147603",
    "SUP-162004"
  ],
  "related_confluence_pages": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/soft-quota-behavior",
    "https://confluence.redwood.ai/postmortems/2025-11-rate-limit-fallout"
  ],
  "description": "Issue summary:\nCustomer reports intermittent inference hangs and long tail latencies starting 2026-03-09 21:00 UTC. Symptoms appear as request timeouts or stalled streaming responses. Customer SDK shows repeated client retries which increase request rate.\n\nImpact:\n- Several production routes for Nimbus Health experienced perceived latency > 30s, many clients closed streams and retried.\n- User-facing workflows (document summarization pipeline) experienced ~12% failure rate during peaks.\n\nEnvironment:\n- Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) in us-west-2 on customer's Dedicated instance.\n- API requests routed through hosted API gateway with rate limiting and soft quota signals enabled for dedicated customers.\n\nSteps to reproduce (reported by customer):\n1) Send a burst of concurrent streaming generation requests (concurrency ~120).\n2) When a subset of requests receive 429s or soft-quota HTTP headers, client SDK retries with exponential backoff but short initial backoff (100ms).\n3) Observed behavior: SDK retries overlap with original traffic window causing repeated 429s and long queuing behind the serving runtime.\n\nObserved behavior:\n- Intermittent 429 responses returned from gateway and occasionally 503 from upstream serving-runtime when queue grows.\n- Client logs show retry storm patterns (batches of identical requests retried every ~200-800ms).\n- Token-level cost spikes correlate with retry windows.\n\nExpected behavior:\n- Soft-quota signals should throttle politely without inducing retry storms that cascade into higher end-to-end latency.\n\nRelevant logs/traces/dashboards:\n- Kibana traces: trace IDs provided by customer (see comments).\n- Console dashboard: route \"nimbus-prod/summarize\" shows latency percentiles and rate-limit counters (dashboard link in comment).\n- Gateway logs indicate 4xx rate-limit code returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining=0 in several sequences.\n\nTemporary workaround (customer applied):\n- Customer reduced client SDK concurrency and increased initial backoff to 800ms which reduced perceived stalls.\n\nPriority justification:\n- Customer-facing degradation affecting critical summarization workflows; dedicated customer on active contract.\n\nRequested action:\n- Determine whether gateway soft-quota signals are being emitted too aggressively for dedicated customers during short bursts.\n- Recommend mitigation: improved headers for retry guidance (Retry-After or explicit soft-quota TTL) and temporary tuning to backoff defaults in customer SDKs.\n",
  "investigation_notes": [
    "2026-03-10 02:10 UTC \u2014 Support replicated pattern using customer's concurrency profile against staging gateway. Observed 4xx responses with no explanatory Retry-After header in several sequences.",
    "2026-03-10 06:45 UTC \u2014 SRE throttling hypothesis: gateway layer is applying burst-window enforcement then falling back to per-account soft quota. Need to check token-bucket config for dedicated pools.",
    "2026-03-10 09:20 UTC \u2014 Correlated spikes in request count with billing meter logs; meter shows transient spike in token consumption consistent with retries, not initial user requests. This implies amplification by client retries.",
    "2026-03-11 11:05 UTC \u2014 Serving runtime queue depth rose to >500ms 95th percentile during retry windows; upstream returned 503 when autoscaler could not provision fast enough for sudden replays.",
    "2026-03-11 14:00 UTC \u2014 Found missing Retry-After header on many 429 responses from the gateway when soft-quota policy triggered. Gateway code path for dedicated pools uses soft-quota signal without setting Retry-After for sub-second suppression.",
    "2026-03-11 16:30 UTC \u2014 Customer reduced concurrency and adjusted SDK backoff; error rate dropped from 12% -> 2% during the same test bursts.",
    "Next steps: add Retry-After to 429 soft-quota responses, evaluate increasing initial suppression window for dedicated pools (config change), and update SDK guidance for backoff defaults."
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2026-03-10 00:40 UTC \u2014 Maria Chen (Support): Thanks for the report. Can you share a sample request ID and the SDK version? Also send a representative trace from Kibana so we can correlate gateway and runtime logs.",
    "2026-03-10 01:05 UTC \u2014 Nimbus Health (Customer): Provided trace IDs: trace-9812, trace-9817. SDK v2.4.1. Added sample request JSON in attachment (see ticket attachments).",
    "2026-03-10 06:55 UTC \u2014 Omar Patel (SRE): Replicated a similar burst against staging; seeing repeated 429s without Retry-After. Opening investigation with gateway team. Routing to component owners: @gateway-team, @serving-runtime.",
    "2026-03-10 12:30 UTC \u2014 Gateway Engineer (internal): Found that soft-quota enforcement for dedicated accounts is using fast-path QoS that emits a custom header X-Soft-Quota-Expires but not Retry-After. Will prototype adding Retry-After values and test rollback window.",
    "2026-03-11 15:10 UTC \u2014 Nimbus Health (Customer): We tested reducing concurrency and increasing backoff \u2014 clear improvement. Happy to run another test once you have a gateway tweak.",
    "2026-03-12 08:00 UTC \u2014 Omar Patel (SRE): Planned change: emit Retry-After=0.8s for soft-quota 429s for dedicated pools and increase burst suppression to 1s. Will schedule rollout to canary tomorrow. Keeping ticket open while we validate."
  ],
  "resolution": "In progress \u2014 mitigation planned. Gateway will emit Retry-After for soft-quota 429s and adjust suppression window for dedicated pools. Customer advised to update SDK backoff defaults as a complementary measure. Post-deployment validation required.",
  "title_field_name": "summary",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "investigation_notes",
    "comments",
    "resolution"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_205c62f1ace8402abf9820662d82ccef"
}

def _get_retry_after_from_exception_header(
    response_headers: Optional[httpx.Headers] = None,
):
    """
    Reimplementation of openai's calculate retry after, since that one can't be imported.
    https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/af67cfab4210d8e497c05390ce14f39105c77519/src/openai/_base_client.py#L631
    """
    try:
        import email  # openai import

        # About the Retry-After header: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After
        #
        # <http-date>". See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Retry-After#syntax for
        # details.
        if response_headers is not None:
            retry_header = response_headers.get("retry-after")
            try:
                retry_after = int(retry_header)
            except Exception:
                retry_date_tuple = email.utils.parsedate_tz(retry_header)  # type: ignore
                if retry_date_tuple is None:
                    retry_after = -1
                else:
                    retry_date = email.utils.mktime_tz(retry_date_tuple)  # type: ignore
                    retry_after = int(retry_date - time.time())
        else:
            retry_after = -1

        return retry_after

    except Exception:
        retry_after = -1


def _calculate_retry_after(
    remaining_retries: int,
    max_retries: int,
    response_headers: Optional[httpx.Headers] = None,
    min_timeout: int = 0,
) -> Union[float, int]:
    retry_after = _get_retry_after_from_exception_header(response_headers)

    # Add some jitter (default JITTER is 0.75 - so upto 0.75s)
    jitter = JITTER * random.random()

    # If the API asks us to wait a certain amount of time (and it's a reasonable amount), just do what it says.
    if retry_after is not None and 0 < retry_after <= 60:
        return retry_after + jitter

    # Calculate exponential backoff
    num_retries = max_retries - remaining_retries
    sleep_seconds = INITIAL_RETRY_DELAY * pow(2.0, num_retries)

    # Make sure sleep_seconds is boxed between min_timeout and MAX_RETRY_DELAY
    sleep_seconds = max(sleep_seconds, min_timeout)
    sleep_seconds = min(sleep_seconds, MAX_RETRY_DELAY)

    return sleep_seconds + jitter
